dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Basic Graph Theory
dossier_meta.statement_text: Problem for every graph $ G $ , we let $ L(G) $ denote the line graph of $ G $ . Given that $ G $ is a tree, can we determine it from the integer sequence $ |V(G)|, |V(L(G))|, |V(L(L(G)))|, \ldots $ ?
dossier_meta.context_text: Graph reconstruction is a notoriously difficult subject. This conjecture is an unusual type of reconstruction problem where our class of graphs is very limited - just trees, but we are also given relatively little information - just a sequence of integers.
dossier_meta.references_text: - [GR] C. Godsil and G. Royle, Algebraic graph theory. Graduate Texts in Mathematics, 207. Springer-Verlag, New York, 2001 (page 18).
